newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Intria sees 70-80 mln rgt pre-tax.
newsitem.headline: Intria sees 70-80 mln rgt pre-tax.

text.p: Malaysian construction group Intria Bhd said on Thursday it expected its pre-tax profit for the year ended June 1997 to be between 70 million ringgit and 80 million ringgit.
Asked for his profit projections following the company's annual general meeting, Azman Firdaus, executive vice chairman of the company said, "between 70 to 80 million" in pre-tax profits.
Azman also said he hopes to turn around U.K. construction and engineering firm Costain Plc, in which it has a 40 percent stake, within one year.
"I intend to turn Costain around within one year," Azman said.
In the previous full-year, Intria reported pre-tax profits of 41.59 million ringgit and turnover of 142.42 million ringgit.
Discussing the rise in pre-tax profits expected in the current financial year, Azman said, "The additional profit will come from construction and the associated companies that we have acquired."
In August, Intria said it was proposing to acquire stakes in construction firms ACP Industries Bhd and FCW Holdings Bhd.
Intria's tie-up with Costain is aimed at providing it with technical know-how.

The U.K. firm reported a loss of 19.2 million pounds in the six months ended June 30, versus a loss of 10.4 million in the year-ago period. Allan Lovell, Costain's chief executive, has said full-year results would be "considerably better" than 1995.
Azman also said Costain is still talking to prospective buyers for its U.S. coal business but did not provide details.
